lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Snow, and silence, and the old Warden road climbing into the pass. Every mile there is a frozen shrine, and a candle nobody has lit in seventy years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pip walks at the front. Nobody agreed that she could come. Nobody managed to stop her, either.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Bree said I could come if I wore two scarves. I'm wearing three. So that's more than allowed.
lines.direction: quick, very pleased with her own logic

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ahead, figures climb the road through the snow: pilgrims in Warden grey, a dwarf with a mason's hammer, a goliath carrying nothing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They are dead. They walk the road they walked in life, and they do not look at you.

options.label: We step off the road and let them pass.
I'll say the pilgrims' rite at the shrine.
That one has my people's clan marks.
Lark taught me a road song for the pass. I'll sing it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The dead walk by close enough to touch. A pilgrim's lips move without a sound, shaping the same word over and over.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: She's saying the name of the next shrine. She's been saying it for seventy years. She doesn't know she already got there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You brush the frost from the shrine and speak the old rite. The words come slowly here, as if the cold were listening.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The pilgrim at the front stops, and bows, and walks on. For a moment she looked as if she remembered why.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His arms carry the clan lines of a hold that froze before you were born. You know the pattern. He doesn't.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: He's looking for his house. He walks up, and it isn't there, so he walks down and tries again.
lines.direction: matter-of-fact, the way children say terrible things

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You sing the road song Lark taught you. The dead don't turn. But at the second verse a small voice joins in, and it knows a third verse you never learned.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pip is singing under her breath: a slow Warden marching song, in words nobody has used for a hundred years.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Up the grey road, keeper, carry the coal. Mind the cold, for the cold minds you.
lines.direction: suddenly old and slow, not a child's cadence at all; half sung

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I don't know that one. I've never heard that one. Why do I keep knowing ones I've never heard?

options.label: It's me, Pip. Hold my hand and tell me what else you know.
Where do you think the songs come from?
Keep singing. The dead seem to like it.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: There's a door at the top of a long stair, with a crack down the middle. I know exactly where the crack is.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: And I'm scared that when we get there, I'll know what's behind it.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Bree says the shard in her hearth eats things. Maybe it ate a song, and got lonely, and gave it to me.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: That's a joke. Mostly.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So she sings. The dead walk on ahead of you, slower now, as if they were keeping time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Near dusk the road turns, and through the snow you see the dark doors of Greyhold, cut into the mountain.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Greyhold. The masons kept their books there. How do I know that?
lines.direction: suddenly old and slow, not a child's cadence at all, then catching herself

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Greyhold is a dwarven road-hold, carved into the mountain and frozen solid. Its doors stand open. Its halls are full of books and ice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the record hall, ledgers climb the walls to the ceiling, each in the careful hand of a mason who wanted to be remembered.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: This is where they drew the Keep, before they built it. I know which shelf.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She is right. On the third shelf from the floor lies a roll of plans, bound in iron and stamped with the Warden seal.

options.label: These are my people's marks. Let me read them.
Those are building plans. I know how to read a plan.
We'll work it out from the ledgers.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The masons wrote in the old dwarven hand, the one you learned from your grandmother's tombstones. You know the word for every kind of stone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The flame hall is drawn with walls nine feet thick, and runes of binding over every lintel. A mason does not bind a hearth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The joints are a smith's joints, the kind Tobin Fell taught you. This hall was built like a lock, not a fireplace.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every wall leans inward. Every door opens out. Whatever burned in there, the hall was built so it could never leave.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ledgers are orders for stone and iron. One is a mason's complaint: the Wardens wanted the flame hall built stronger than the gate.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ledgers blur into orders for stone and lime. Then Pip pulls one free and opens it at a drawing without looking, as if someone had shown her the page.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the last page of the plans, in the margin, a mason has written a note in a shaking hand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: We were told to build a hearth. We have built a cage. Gods forgive us if the thing inside ever wakes and wants to go home.
lines.direction: read as the mason's words, quiet and ashamed

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: It hums, in there. It always hummed. I used to think that meant it was happy.
lines.direction: suddenly old and slow, not a child's cadence at all

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I never used to think anything. I've never been there. Stop looking at me like that.
lines.direction: quick and defensive, a child again

options.label: The Skarrow song said the seven came back running. A cage for something stolen.
What would a fire need a cage for?
Corvin needs to see this. I'll copy every page.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The pieces sit together like stones in a wall: something taken from beyond the Greywall, and a hall built so that it could never leave.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody has an answer. Somewhere far below, in the dark of the hold, the ice cracks like a door.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You copy the plans by candle, fingers numb, and never once by ember-light. Some things should not be read by a fire that eats.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When you leave, the dead are waiting at the gate of the hold, all facing the caves above the pass. Something up there is pulling at them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And above the caves, a single window in an old watchtower burns with a cold blue light.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The caves of the cold ember are crystal and blue ice, lit from somewhere deep inside. It is the coldest place you have ever stood.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kobolds work the walls with picks under lamps of pale fire. Each wears the same stitched badge: a tower, and a closed eye.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Something large shifts in the webs above them. The kobolds see you, drop their picks, and take up their slings.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: They're not dead ones. They're alive ones. That's worse, isn't it?

options.label: The cold here is wrong. It isn't winter. Something has stopped.
Those wards on the walls are necromancy, and fresh.
Pip, get behind the rocks and stay there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You listen to the mountain and hear nothing at all. No water, no roots. The land is holding its breath, and has been for seventy years.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wards are careful, elegant work, written to keep the dead out of the caves, not in. Whoever wrote them is protecting something.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I'm behind the rocks. I'm staying. I'm only looking a little bit.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The first sling-stone cracks against the ice beside you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The caves fall quiet. The kobolds who are left flee up a stair cut into the ice, and at the top of it a door is opening.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: That will do. They're paid to dig, not to die. Come up, all of you, before your fingers go black.
lines.direction: soft and tired, a doctor's calm

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The man in the doorway is thin and grey, in a physician's coat stiff with frost. He holds the door like someone used to patients arriving hurt.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: My name is Ivo Rime. You've come for the cold ember, I expect.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Come in and get warm first. Then we can argue.

options.label: We'll come in. Slowly.
Is this a trap? I'll watch him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There is no trap in him. Only a man who hasn't slept properly in a very long time, and has stopped expecting anyone to be kind.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You can't read him. His face gives you nothing but tiredness, and the patience of a man used to delivering bad news.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Mind the third step. It's ice all the way down. Everything here is.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Only one room in the tower is warm. A brazier burns beside a narrow bed, and on the bed lies a woman, still and pale, in a grey dress.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Sit. No, there, by the fire. You've been breathing cold air for days. I can hear it in your chests.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: This is Nell, my wife. She died in the hungry years, of a fever I could have treated, if we'd had anything to treat it with.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: I brought her up here because the cold ember raises the dead. It does. She walked, for a while. She didn't know my name.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: They walk, but they don't remember. I wanted to know where the remembering went. I think I know now.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Fire keeps what it burns. A cold ember still holds every memory it ever took. They're only frozen, like everything else up here.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Warm it, just a little, with a living ember, and I believe I can give a person back what the fire took from them.
lines.direction: a flicker of excitement he can't quite hide

options.label: What do you need from us?
Will this actually work? Let me see her.
Could you put back the memory we paid the Glimmer Court?
Show me your notes.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: One of the embers you carry, set against the cold one, for the length of a breath. I'll pay what the fire takes. It's my use, not yours.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: And then I'll know whether I've spent eleven years on a cure or on a cruelty.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His method is sound. But she has been dead for years. He might give her memories back. He can't give them anywhere to stay.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Yes. I know. A minute, perhaps. I would take a minute.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His notes are dense and careful and far beyond you. You only understand that he believes it, and that he stopped sleeping to keep believing it.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: No. I'm sorry. The fire keeps what it burns. The Court doesn't burn, it eats. There's nothing of yours left to put back.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Whoever paid: write down everything you remember around the gap. It helps. It's what I'd tell any patient.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The notes are a doctor's case files. Nell's pulse, Nell's colour, how far Nell walked each day she walked. Eleven years of a single patient.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The last page says only: if this fails, stop. Underlined twice.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Mister Rime. If you can put memories back into people, can you take them out?

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Out of whom, child?

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Me. I've got ones that aren't mine. Songs, and roads, and a man who's very tired. I don't want to carry him around any more.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ivo kneels in front of her, the way a doctor does, so that his eyes are level with hers.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: I could try. I won't. Whoever they were, the fire burned them away, and you're the only place they're still kept.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: That's heavy. But it isn't a sickness. It's a debt the dead ran up, and it isn't yours to pay alone.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: All right.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: So. Will you let me try? If you say no, I'll fight you for it. I'm sorry. I'm too tired to pretend I wouldn't.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nell lies still on the narrow bed. The brazier ticks. Below the tower, the dead of the pass have gathered in the snow, waiting for nothing.

options.label: Let him try.
Stop him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You set the ember against the cold one. For one breath the caves glow gold, and every dead thing on the mountain turns its head.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nell opens her eyes.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Nell?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She looks at him for a long time. Then she smiles, the way people smile at someone who is late, and forgiven.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She lifts a hand to his face and says his name, once. Then the light goes out of her, gently, and this time she does not walk again.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Thank you. That was a minute. I said I would take a minute.
lines.direction: a long pause first, then very steady

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: I'm done with the Kindled. Maren wanted the cold ember lit. It's yours. And whatever else I have, if you ever need a doctor.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: I can't remember her mother's name. The fire took it. Nell would laugh. She never liked her mother.
lines.direction: trying for a joke, and nearly managing

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Ah. Yes. I thought you might. You have honest faces.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He fights like a doctor, which is to say he knows exactly where it hurts, and he hates every moment of it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It is over quickly. His notes go into your packs. The cold ember, dull and blue in its cave, is yours to carry.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Leave her the brazier. Please. She never liked the cold.
lines.direction: on the floor, not trying to get up

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: We'll leave it. I'll leave a scarf as well. One of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When you go, he is sitting by the bed, holding her hand. Maren Sorrel has lost her scholar, and Ivo Rime has nothing left to try.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You make camp in the lee of a frozen shrine below the pass. The fire is small, and it is wood. Nobody reaches for ember-light any more.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the middle of the night, Pip wakes up screaming.

options.label: I'm here, Pip. It's me. Tell me first.
Hold her until she stops shaking.
I'll pray over her, quietly, until she's calm.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: You came. You always come. Don't let them all hear yet. Just you, first.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The others wait at the edge of the firelight while she whispers it into your shoulder. Then she lets you bring them close.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She fights you for a moment, then holds on as hard as she can. Her hands are burning hot, in the coldest place in the Vale.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your prayer is quiet and old. Her breathing slows to the rhythm of it. Your gift asks nothing of her except to listen.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I was a man. I was old, and I was in the Keep, in the big hall, and the fire was in front of me, and it was singing.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I am Oswin Hale, Warden-Keeper. I have read the oldest books. The fire is not ours, and it is eating us.
lines.direction: suddenly old and slow, not a child's cadence at all; another voice entirely

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I am putting it out. Slowly, like a lamp. It is going down, and going quiet, and it is nearly done.
lines.direction: suddenly old and slow, not a child's cadence at all

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: And then someone grabbed his hand. My hand. Someone in a hood, with a cold hand, and they pulled it back.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: And the fire went everywhere. It broke and flew out of the windows like birds. And he was screaming. I was screaming.

options.label: Did you see the face under the hood?
Old Maud said she saw the Stranger's face that night.
Oswin Hale. Corvin reads his letters. He was the last Keeper.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: No face. Just the hood, and the hand. And a voice that said, not like this. Like it was sorry.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: I didn't see a face. Only a hood. Lots of people have hoods.
lines.direction: too quickly; a lie, or a hope

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Oswin Hale: the name at the foot of half the letters in Corvin's archive, the Keeper who swore never to touch the fire. A century gone.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: He was so tired. He's still tired. I can feel it, like a cold in the next room.
lines.direction: suddenly old and slow, not a child's cadence at all, fading back

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: Can I sleep next to someone? Not because I'm scared. Because it's cold.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: When you go to the Keep, I'm coming. Don't say no. I know the way in. He does, so I do.
lines.direction: quick and stubborn, then suddenly old and slow

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: High on the dark ridge above the camp, a hooded figure stands and watches the fire, and does not come down.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ivo Rime comes down from his tower at first light, a doctor's bag over his shoulder and nothing else.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: I heard her from the tower. Sound carries up here. Let me look at her. No, I'm not asking.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Pulse fast. Temperature high, for this cold. Nothing wrong with her that sleep and soup won't mend.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: The memory, though. That isn't going anywhere. Somebody very old put it in very deep.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: You can stay, if you want. You're less sad than yesterday.

lines.speaker: ivo_rime
lines.text: Am I? Well. Doctor's orders, then. I'll see you all down the mountain. After that, keep her warm.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the morning you look back up the pass. The window in Rime's tower is still lit: a single cold blue light.

lines.speaker: pip_ashdown
lines.text: He's still sitting with her. I know it. Not the fire way. Just the ordinary knowing way.
